chapters.title: Chapter 5: Trading Mechanics, Risk and Tax

lessons.title: How Currency Derivative Profits Are Taxed in India

children.text: Rhea ends the year with ₹1,20,000 of profitable EUR/USD futures trades and ₹40,000 of losing ones. Her colleague tells her to report it as short-term capital gains, like shares. Another says currency trading is "speculation" taxed separately. A third says losses can cut the tax on her salary. All three are wrong. Currency derivatives traded on a recognised Indian exchange have their own tax treatment, and getting it wrong can mean paying the wrong tax, losing the right to carry forward losses, or missing an audit requirement. This lesson covers how that income is classified, how to compute it, how turnover and audits work, what happens to losses, and what changed with the Income-tax Act, 2025.

body.text: Profits from currency futures and options on NSE or BSE are non-speculative business income, not capital gains. They are taxed at your slab rate, losses follow business-loss rules, and your trading turnover, not your profit, decides whether a tax audit applies.

markDefs.definition: Business income that the law does not treat as speculative. Eligible derivatives traded on a recognised stock exchange fall in this category, so their profits and losses follow normal business rules.
Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the single 12-month period from 1 April to 31 March in which income is earned and reported. It replaces the earlier 'previous year' and 'assessment year' terms.

children.text: Under the Income-tax Act, 1961, eligible derivative transactions carried out on a recognised stock exchange were specifically excluded from the definition of a speculative transaction in section 43(5). That made them

, taxed under the head "Profits and Gains of Business or Profession." The Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026, keeps the same treatment under reorganised sections and replaces "previous year" and "assessment year" with a single
. Currency futures and options on NSE and BSE are derivatives in this sense, so the same rules apply to them.

body.title: Name the head of income
body.question: Rhea, a salaried engineer, trades EUR/USD cross-currency futures on NSE and makes a net profit for the year. How is this profit taxed?
options: As short-term capital gains at a special rate
As non-speculative business income at her slab rate
It is tax-free because it was earned in dollars
body.explanation: Currency derivatives on a recognised exchange are excluded from the definition of speculative transactions, so the profit is non-speculative business income taxed at her slab rate. The dollar calculation does not matter: the profit is settled and taxed in rupees.

children.text: Because it is business income, you are taxed on net profit: all trading profits minus all trading losses, minus expenses incurred to earn that income. Typical allowable expenses include brokerage, exchange transaction charges, SEBI fees, stamp duty, GST on those charges, trading software and data subscriptions, and a reasonable share of internet costs. Keep invoices and your broker's contract notes and tax P&L report.

body.title: Tax on Rhea's trading income
body.prompt: Rhea's salary already puts her in the 30% tax bracket. Her taxable currency trading income is ₹74,000. Including 4% health and education cess, and ignoring surcharge, how much extra tax does this income add?
body.explanation: Effective rate = 30% × 1.04 = 31.2%. Tax = ₹74,000 × 31.2% = ₹23,088. Because trading income is added to her other income, it is taxed at her highest slab rate. Someone with a lower total income would pay a lower rate on the same trading profit.

markDefs.definition: For derivatives trading, turnover is the sum of the absolute values of profits and losses on each trade, following the ICAI Guidance Note on Tax Audit. It is not the contract value traded.

children.text: Derivative traders do not measure turnover as the value of contracts traded. Following the ICAI Guidance Note on Tax Audit,

is the sum of the absolute profit or loss on each trade, ignoring whether it was a profit or a loss. Since the 2022 edition of the Guidance Note, premium received on selling options is no longer added to this turnover. Turnover matters because it decides whether a tax audit is required.

body.latex: \text{Trading turnover} = \sum \left| \text{Profit or loss on each trade} \right|
body.caption: Add every trade's result as a positive number

body.title: Work out turnover
body.prompt: Rhea's first five trades result in +₹12,000, minus ₹8,500, +₹4,200, minus ₹15,300 and +₹9,600. What is her trading turnover for these five trades, in rupees?
body.explanation: Turnover = 12,000 + 8,500 + 4,200 + 15,300 + 9,600 = ₹49,600. Her net profit on the same trades is only ₹2,000. Turnover is always at least as large as the absolute net result, and for active traders it is usually much larger.

body.text: A common myth among retail traders is that any F&O loss forces a tax audit. It does not. For most individuals trading entirely through banks and brokers, the turnover threshold is ₹10 crore, far above what a typical retail currency trader reaches. The trap to watch is the presumptive taxation scheme: having used it in earlier years can make an audit necessary when you later report a loss or low profit.

body.caption: Set-off and carry forward of a non-speculative business loss

cells: Can it reduce tax on salary in the same year?
No
Can it be set off against other business income in the same year?
Yes
Can it be set off against other heads such as interest income or capital gains in the same year?
Generally yes, except salary
What happens to the unabsorbed loss?
Carried forward for up to 8 years, against business income only
Is there a condition for carrying it forward?
The return must be filed by the due date. A belated return loses the carry forward.

body.title: The loss that stays with you
body.prompt: In a bad year, Rhea has a net currency trading loss of ₹1,50,000 after expenses. Her other income is a salary of ₹18,00,000 and fixed deposit interest of ₹40,000. If she files her return on time, how much of the trading loss is carried forward to future years, in rupees?
body.explanation: The loss cannot be set off against her salary. It can be set off against the ₹40,000 of interest income, leaving ₹1,50,000 minus ₹40,000 = ₹1,10,000 to carry forward. That amount can reduce tax only on future business income, such as future trading profits, for up to eight years.

body.text: Many salaried traders expect a trading loss to bring them a tax refund on their salary. It will not, because business losses cannot be set off against salary income. And if you miss the return filing due date, you lose the right to carry the loss forward at all. If you have a trading loss, filing on time is the single most valuable tax decision you will make that year.

body.title: A note for businesses that hedge

children.text: When an exporter like Priya or an importer like Karthik uses currency futures, forwards or options to hedge genuine business receivables or payments, the gains and losses on those hedges are generally part of the business's own income, alongside the exchange differences on the underlying invoices. The exact timing and accounting, especially for positions still open at the end of the tax year and for companies following Indian Accounting Standards, can be technical. Businesses should keep clear records linking each hedge to its underlying exposure and take advice from their chartered accountant.

markDefs.definition: Income tax paid in instalments during the year, rather than all at the end, when the expected tax liability after TDS is ₹10,000 or more.

children.text: Your employer deducts tax on your salary, but no one deducts tax on your trading profits. If your total tax after TDS is expected to be ₹10,000 or more, you must pay
in instalments, or pay interest on the shortfall. Trading income is lumpy, so review your profits each quarter before the instalment dates.

events.title: First instalment
events.description: At least 15% of the year's estimated tax.

events.title: Final instalment
events.description: 100% of the estimated tax for the year.

body.title: Rhea's year-end tax plan
body.scenario: It is March. Over the tax year, Rhea made 140 EUR/USD futures trades on NSE. Her broker's tax P&L report shows gross profits of ₹3,10,000 and gross losses of ₹3,45,000. She spent ₹18,000 on brokerage and charges and ₹6,000 on a charting subscription. Her salary is ₹22,00,000, and she also earned ₹25,000 of savings and FD interest. She has never used the presumptive taxation scheme. Her friend says: "You made a loss, so just don't mention trading in your return. Nobody will check."
body.prompt: Work out Rhea's net trading result and turnover, decide whether an audit applies, explain how the loss is treated, and evaluate her friend's advice.
body.modelAnswer:
1. Net trading result: ₹3,10,000 minus ₹3,45,000 = minus ₹35,000, and after expenses of ₹24,000, a net business loss of ₹59,000.
2. Turnover: the sum of absolute trade results is ₹3,10,000 + ₹3,45,000 = ₹6,55,000, far below the ₹10 crore threshold. With no presumptive scheme history, a tax audit is not required just because of the loss.
3. Loss treatment: the ₹59,000 loss cannot reduce tax on her ₹22,00,000 salary. It can be set off against the ₹25,000 of interest income, leaving ₹34,000 to carry forward for up to eight years against future business income.
4. Filing: she must report the trading activity in the return form applicable to business income, not the simple salaried-person form, and file by the due date, or she loses the carry forward.
5. Her friend's advice is wrong. All trades are reported by the exchange and broker, omitting business income is non-compliance, and hiding the loss would also throw away its tax value. Given the sums involved, a quick consultation with a chartered accountant is worthwhile.

body.title: Year-end tax checklist for currency derivative traders
steps: Download your broker's tax P&L report and contract notes for the full tax year.
Separate currency and equity derivative income from any delivery-based capital gains and intraday equity trades.
Total your allowable expenses with invoices.
Calculate turnover as the sum of absolute trade results and check the audit threshold.
Confirm whether you used the presumptive scheme in any of the last five years.
Check your advance tax payments against your final liability.
File the return applicable to business income by the due date, especially if you have a loss to carry forward.

body.label: Income Tax Department e-Filing Portal
body.description: File your return, pay advance tax, check tax credits and view the current return forms and due dates.

body.title: The carry forward period
body.textWithBlank: A non-speculative business loss from derivative trading can be carried forward for up to ___ years, if the return is filed on time.
body.explanation: The unabsorbed loss can be carried forward for eight years and set off only against business income in those years.

cards.definition: The tax head for profits on derivatives traded on recognised exchanges, including currency futures and options.
The 1 April to 31 March period under the Income-tax Act, 2025, replacing previous year and assessment year.
Sum of absolute profits and losses on each trade, per the ICAI Guidance Note. Used for audit thresholds.
₹10 crore of turnover when cash receipts and payments are each within 5%.
Not against salary. Unabsorbed loss is carried forward 8 years against business income if the return is filed on time.
Payable in four instalments when tax after TDS is ₹10,000 or more: 15%, 45%, 75% and 100% by 15 June, September, December and March.

points: Currency futures and options on NSE and BSE produce non-speculative business income, not capital gains, taxed at your slab rate.
The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026 and keeps this treatment, using the new term tax year.
Tax is on net profit after trading losses and allowable expenses such as brokerage, charges and software.
Trading turnover is the sum of absolute results on each trade. The audit threshold is ₹10 crore for largely digital traders, and a loss alone does not trigger an audit.
Business losses cannot be set off against salary. Unabsorbed losses carry forward for 8 years against business income, but only if the return is filed on time.
Pay advance tax if trading profits push your liability after TDS to ₹10,000 or more.
Offshore forex app profits are still taxable, and the activity itself breaches FEMA.

body.text: This lesson is for general education only and is not tax or legal advice. Tax law changed with the Income-tax Act, 2025 from 1 April 2026, and section numbers, return forms, thresholds and due dates can change through Budgets, rules and notifications. Figures in the examples are illustrative and ignore surcharge and other special situations. Consult a qualified chartered accountant before filing your return or making tax decisions.
